facts.text: Mormon pioneers first settled Avon in 1860, originally naming the community Paradise before it was temporarily abandoned in 1868.
Avon was renamed by settler Orson Smith's wife to honor the English town that served as the birthplace of William Shakespeare.
Early settlers chose the site of Avon for its abundant water resources at the forks of East Creek and the Little Bear River.
Pioneers in Avon originally built log homes and dugouts in a defensive fort formation to protect themselves and their livestock.
A post office called Avon operated in the community from 1894 until 1919.
Avon remains focused on agriculture today, with farms producing crops and livestock suited to the valley's mild climate.
